transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

The common causes are a partially closed tap, kinked hose or blocked inlet mesh; less commonly the AquaStop safety hose, inlet valve or fill sensing. 1. Switch the dishwasher off. Check the water tap feeding it is fully open and that the inlet hose is not trapped or kinked behind the machine. This is the quickest and most common fix. 2. If the hose has a larger safety/AquaStop box at the tap end, look for damage or a red indicator window. A red indication can mean the hose safety device has operated. 3. Isolate the water at the tap, put a towel down, then unscrew the inlet hose from the dishwasher end. Look into the connection for the small mesh strainer. Rinse off any grit or limescale, refit the hose securely, turn the tap back on and try a programme. If the tap, hose and mesh are all clear but it still gives 4C without taking water, the likely next suspects are the inlet valve or the fill/flow sensing, which is usually an engineer repair. Also, if it is continually running a drain-pump noise even though the tub is empty, stop trying to run it: that can indicate water in the base tray triggering flood protection rather than a normal supply fault.

I checked under the sink. The hose has no kinks. The valve feeding the dishwasher is a screwdriver-slot type and the slot is at 90 degrees to the pipe, so I think it's turned off. A plumber fitted a new kitchen tap yesterday. Should I turn it on?

Yes — on the usual screwdriver-slot isolation valve, the slot being across the pipe means closed; parallel with the pipe means open. The new tap work makes this the most likely reason for the 4C water-supply error. Turn the slot one quarter-turn so it runs in line with the pipe. Do not force it if it is stiff. Check for any drips under the sink, then start a programme. If it now fills, the fault was simply the closed supply valve. If 4C returns with the valve open, the next most likely issue is debris from the plumbing work caught in the dishwasher inlet mesh; after that, an inlet valve/fill-sensing fault would need investigating.
Ok, I turned the valve so the slot runs in line with the pipe and started a programme. It's filling and running normally now, no drips.

That has resolved it: the dishwasher’s water supply isolation valve had been left closed after the tap work, which caused the 4C water-supply error. As it is now filling, running normally and there are no drips, no further repair is needed. For future reference, the slot on that type of valve is normally parallel with the pipe when open and across it when closed. Is there anything else you would like help with?
